provenance: Original snippets and explanations authored for CollegeHubs; no third-party snippets.

review.method: Static review of intended behavior, unique correct choice and explanation; snippets are never executed.

puzzles.explanation: Array indices end at length - 1. The <= condition also reads items[length], producing an extra undefined value.

puzzles.prompt: Sort these numbers in ascending numeric order.
puzzles.explanation: Without a comparator, JavaScript sort compares string forms. A numeric comparator orders 2, 3, 10 correctly.
A block-bodied arrow function needs an explicit return. Without it, map receives undefined for every element.

puzzles.prompt: Enter the branch only when attempts is zero.
puzzles.explanation: Assignment changes attempts to zero and evaluates to zero, which is falsy. Strict equality checks the value without changing it.

puzzles.prompt: Read two decimal integer strings and add them.
puzzles.explanation: The + operator concatenates these strings into "123". Converting both known integer strings to numbers gives 15.
Assignment shares the same object. A shallow copy is sufficient here because name is a primitive string, so changing the copy preserves the original.
Both bounds must hold. With OR, any ordinary numeric age satisfies at least one side, so ages outside the range are accepted.

puzzles.prompt: Sum all entries, including when the array is empty.
puzzles.explanation: An uninitialized variable is undefined. Adding a number to it produces NaN. Starting at zero also returns the correct sum for an empty array.
